# wherdr v3 documentation

> wherdr is a web app to start coding agents on herdr-core (hc), follow their work and answer
> them from a phone. Read this index first, then only the section that answers your question.
> Links are relative to the repository root. A section that starts with "Needs:" makes sense only
> with the section it names: read that one too.

## Start here

- [Documentation home](docs/README.md): the list of pages, v3 and v2 only.
- [Overview](docs/overview.md#why-wherdr): what wherdr does for you.
- [How it works](docs/overview.md#how-it-works): wherdr's server, the hc socket, transcripts and the data folder.
- [herdr-core](docs/core.md): what v3 supports on hc, the reference for inventory, terminals and conversations.
- [First launch](docs/quick-start.md#quick-start): build, start and open wherdr from source; Settings › About shows `wherdr <version>+<commit> · herdr-core`; Alfred and the setup window set up a first project; then the Board, or Alfred.

## Install and update

- [Requirements](docs/installation.md#requirements): hc, Linux or macOS, Node.js 22 and Git.
- [The hc socket](docs/installation.md#the-hc-socket): the default `HC_SOCKET`: `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/herdr-core/<session>.sock` on Linux, `~/.local/state/herdr-core/<session>/<session>.sock` on macOS; session `default`.
- [v2 and v3 on one computer](docs/installation.md#v2-and-v3-on-one-computer): v2 and a by-hand v3 both default to port 7683; start v3 with `PORT=7684`.
- [On macOS](docs/installation.md#on-macos): install by hand (the script needs systemd), the macOS socket path, a LaunchAgent, Keep awake.
- [Installation](docs/installation.md#installation): install v3 and run it as a service.
- [Keep it running](docs/installation.md#keep-it-running): run wherdr as a service (a systemd --user unit, a macOS LaunchAgent).
- [On-device dictation files](docs/installation.md#on-device-dictation-files): where the dictation models and read-aloud voices are fetched and kept.
- [Updating](docs/installation.md#updating): the version in Settings › About (with its commit), a banner for a newer 3.x release only (never a 2.x) with What's new (the release notes) and Update with Alfred, or update v3 by hand.
- [Update with an agent](docs/update-with-an-agent.md): the steps Alfred (or any agent) follows to update v3: find the unit, read the release's Upgrade notes, plan and your yes, back up DATA_DIR, update.sh or git pull/npm ci/npm run build, check /api/health, roll back on failure; never sudo without asking, never restart herdr-core.
- [Install with an agent](docs/install-with-an-agent.md): ready-to-paste prompts for an agent that installs or updates wherdr.
- [Release notes 3.0.0](docs/release-notes-3.0.0.md): what v3 brings to a v2 user: projects, board and coordinators (named after their project, row menu, Read/Act on other projects), New project with no template step, Tasks to review, Accept at any time, Notes, the merge queue and engine reliability, Alfred's one-card v2 import, quotas, phone fixes, the update banner (What's new, Update with Alfred, Upgrade notes); what changed (installed from the v3 branch beside v2, GitHub release only), what is gone, how to move; workspaces come in 3.1.
- [What v3 drops](docs/release-notes-3.0.0.md#gone-v2-only): what v3 drops compared with v2: Herdr sessions and plugin, the herdr-projects board, npm, Homebrew, curl installer, Docker, one-tap update, worktrees, model pickers, split panes.
- [Migrate from v2](docs/migrate-from-v2.md): install v3 beside v2 and import its machines, settings and recent folders, nothing of herdr-projects; Alfred sets up its projects.
- [What is imported](docs/migrate-from-v2.md#what-is-imported): what the v2 import brings over (v2's own machine becomes v3's local one in the machine tabs and groups), and what to redo.
- [Set up your v2 projects with Alfred](docs/migrate-from-v2.md#set-up-your-v2-projects-with-alfred): Alfred's first message offers to bring v2 projects over, reading the herdr-projects board then: one card lists them all (a checkbox each, a folder not found says why, and Start their coordinators), and one Apply adds the checked ones and starts their coordinators, no workflow needed (each coordinator's first reply proposes a workflow); then per project its open tasks (under-way ones continue from their branch and PR); an optional handover note from the v2 coordinator and its autopilot goal go into the new coordinator's memory.md.
- [Auto-deploy from a build machine](docs/migrate-from-v2.md#auto-deploy-from-a-build-machine): build elsewhere and deploy to the server.
- [Fall back to v2](docs/migrate-from-v2.md#fall-back-to-v2): go back to v2, and [uninstall v3](docs/migrate-from-v2.md#uninstall-v3); on v3, `herdr plugin install|update` and the `curl … | sh` installer change nothing and say how to install v3.
- [Install as an app](docs/phone.md#install-it-as-an-app): add wherdr to a phone's home screen or a desktop browser.
- [App start](docs/phone.md#app-start): Settings › Phone › App start, network first or saved copy first; after an update, a Reload banner and no reload by itself.

## Network and security

- [Tailscale setup](docs/networks.md#recommended-always-on-server--tailscale): reach wherdr from a phone over a tailnet with HTTPS.
- [Other private networks](docs/networks.md#other-private-networks): Headscale, NetBird, ZeroTier or WireGuard instead.
- [Security](docs/security.md#security): who may reach wherdr, the passkey lock and remote-shell risks.
- [Network access](docs/security.md#network-access): which networks wherdr answers, and `WHERDR_TRUSTED_NETWORKS`.
- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md#configuration): environment variables (`WHERDR_ROOT`: the install folder, where Alfred finds the running build's docs) and the data folder.
- [Settings beside the conversation](docs/configuration.md#settings-beside-the-conversation): on a computer window at least 1280 px wide, Settings opened from a conversation show as a side panel on the linked section, resizable from its left edge (drag, arrows, double-click for the default; width kept on the device); Escape closes it, Open full page keeps the full page; `&target=<id>` scrolls to one setting and outlines it for a few seconds.

## Agent list

- [Alfred](docs/home.md#alfred): wherdr's assistant (its card looks selected only while its conversation is open), its agent (kept until you change it), name, home folder and memory; with no project, its first message and Home's empty list offer to set up the first one (with Alfred or in the setup window).
- [Agents on herdr-core](docs/home.md#agents-on-herdr-core): the live list, states and their counters (agent rows plus the tab's coordinators), quick answers, the sidebar's order (no sideways scroll: long titles and badges ellipsized, a thin scrollbar), and task agents named after their task (after a restart too), one row per task with a line per agent (its agent's icon, role, machine, last message; a reviewer's verdict as a short line, not JSON).
- [Coordinators](docs/home.md#coordinators): project coordinator rows under Alfred, with the project's colored key badge and the coordinator's name (the project's by default, renamable in the General tab and at setup), and their menu (open the board, project settings, autopilot with its on check, rename inline, mute, restart with another agent, stop after a confirm); a stopped one (its terminal ended) offers to resume its conversation or start a new one; coordinators and Tasks to review follow the machine tab (a project shows on the tabs holding its machines, Alfred on every tab).
- [Tasks to review](docs/home.md#tasks-to-review): Home's card with the count of what waits for you on the tab's projects and the ids of the first ones as colored key badges on one line (… past it); a tap opens them one at a time.
- [Offered agents](docs/home.md#offered-agents): Settings › Agents, which programs every picker offers and in which order.
- [Machines as tabs](docs/home.md#machines-as-tabs): the machine tabs and their counts (rows and coordinators), their groups (deleting one puts its projects back to Automatic), which tabs show a project (its machines', a paused one only while its task runs, or its Shown in; notifications are not filtered, the board only on Follow machine tab), a machine's actions, and the offline machines' line with Reconnect (no machine chips while all are online).
- [New agents and tabs](docs/home.md#new-agents-and-tabs): the New sheet (its machine: the current tab's first online one, else the host, as on All), the + of a space's tabs, and renaming or closing a tab or a space.
- [Search](docs/home.md#search): search agents and conversations.
- [Notes panel](docs/home.md#notes): the header's Notes button (Mod+Alt+P): the agents' notes, read-only, beside the conversation or Home's list on a computer of 1280 px or more (resizable), a sheet otherwise; Follow tab by default (a muted line names the tab followed, another says when it has no note of its own), or All or one tab (a group or a machine shown as its own tab); checkboxes, project and custom badges, in-app links and links between notes; a linked file (plans/x.md) opens rendered in the panel with a back arrow, its relative links kept inside the notes folder; missing links muted with a tooltip; live updates.
- [Inventory](docs/core.md#inventory): how terminals are placed in spaces and tabs, and how states are read.
- [Creating terminals and agents, machines](docs/core.md#creating-terminals-and-agents-machines): what the New sheet asks hc to run, and how hc reaches core machines.
- [Agent actions](docs/core.md#agent-actions): the agent's … menu: rename, keep after restart, answers, attachments.

## Conversation, terminal and files

- [Conversation and replies](docs/conversation.md): transcripts, following new messages from the bottom, one-tap answers, choice buttons (1 to 4, one alone is a confirm; an invalid block stays code) and live task cards (`task KEY-12`, opens the task's sheet) from a `wherdr` code fence, quoted replies, attachments (shown as chips once sent, photos as pictures also after Send now / Retry), messages sent while a wake is typed waiting for it instead of failing, dictation, and in-app links (`#/settings?section=…`, `#/board?task=…`), shown as labelled buttons, that open a place in wherdr.
- [Live status cards](docs/conversation.md#live-status-cards): a `wherdr` code fence of `status machine:<key>`, `status quota:claude|codex`, `status pr:<KEY>#<n>` or `status op:<task id>` lines shows live cards from wherdr's own data, refreshed every 15 s on screen, "unavailable" when the source is gone.
- [Places an agent opens for you](docs/conversation.md#places-an-agent-opens-for-you): `wherdr alfred ui open` / `wherdr pm ui open '<in-app link>'` shows a place on the device the user last used on the agent's conversation (Settings side panel on a wide computer, even for bare `#/settings`), says where (phone or computer), keeps the card in the reply (```wherdr `open <link>`), the one element for the place (a bar as wide as the message field only when the reply ends without it), only in a turn from the user, changing nothing; `ui open --target <id>` highlights one setting (`ui targets` lists the ids; a part of a project's sheet, `project.workflow|guards|autopilot`, takes `--project <KEY>`).
- [Buttons an agent puts in its reply](docs/conversation.md#buttons-an-agent-puts-in-its-reply): `wherdr pm ui action resume|step|open <task>` adds a card with *Resume*, the step's own button (*Merge*, *Approve screenshots*) or *Open*; only the user's click runs it (`POST /api/ui/act`, never a token), through the task sheet's handlers, after checking the task still waits the same way (else *This changed since*, nothing runs); only in a turn from the user; the outcome shows on the card (an approved merge not ready yet: approved, merges once ready; a refused step action keeps the button with its reason). Settings: `wherdr alfred setting set <key> <value> --propose` adds a card (before → after, *Show me* highlights it, *Cancel*, *Apply*); only the user's Apply changes it, stale if the setting moved since; Alfred never applies a setting itself. Project changes: `wherdr alfred project add|template|guards|machine … --propose` or `coordinator start … --propose` adds the same card with the change's lines; Apply makes it only while its dry run still shows those lines. [What a card tells its agent](docs/conversation.md#what-a-card-tells-its-agent): Apply, Cancel or a failed apply (and a workflow or automation change answered) is typed into the proposer's conversation as a muted *From the card* row (`From the card: Applied: <summary>`, `Cancelled: …`, `Not applied: <why>`), as the user's turn, so it goes on by itself; while it does not run, its next start's first message lists them. `wherdr pm ui show file <path>|shots <task>` shows a file of the agent's own folder or a task's screenshots (before/after) in the side panel, or a card then a sheet on a phone; it approves nothing.
- [Conversations on hc](docs/core.md#conversations): which agents open on their transcript and how it is read, and text left unsent in Claude's input box (a photo message is submitted once Claude shows its placeholders, retried once; never shown as read, never glued to the next message).
- [Terminal](docs/terminal.md): the real terminal, shared viewers and taking control.
- [Files](docs/files.md): browse an agent's folder, preview text, Markdown, images, PDFs and videos, download; which files a path in a conversation may open.
- [On a computer](docs/devices.md#on-a-computer): layout, terminal key bar and keyboard shortcuts.
- [On a phone](docs/devices.md#on-a-phone): touch controls and the phone keybar (order and hidden keys in Settings › Terminal).
- [On an iPad](docs/devices.md#on-an-ipad): the iPad layout.

## Project management

- [Projects](docs/project-management.md#projects): Settings › Projects, the project list (grey blocks until it is read, Try again if that fails) and the project sheet's tabs (wide on a computer, General fields side by side).
- [Getting started](docs/project-management.md#getting-started): the setup window, three steps (Turn on, with Let Alfred guide me a quieter button; Your project: folder, machine, visibility and the coordinator's agent and model (empty: the agent's default), kept as its default; Meet your coordinator: Start with… starts it and opens its conversation, its first message proposing how you work), no Back on the first step, no workflow or template to pick (the coordinator's first message proposes the first workflow, guards included; templates stay in the Workflow tab); a project counts as set up once its coordinator runs, with or without a workflow; step 3 says starting, asks with Answer its question, or runs, and Next waits until it runs; the coordinator's and Alfred's new folder trusted at their first start; what a project needs (git, and `origin` unless its workflow lands locally like vibe); the coordinator's own memory.md; Finish setup on the board; New › Project opens on adding one (machine tabs, the machine's git repositories with a search, Or any folder with Browse; picking one fills name and key, editable, shown as ~/…; no template: the minimal default, its coordinator starts at once with the chosen agent and proposes a workflow; below, Existing projects lists only those whose coordinator does not run, hidden when none; a wider sheet on a computer).
- [The coordinator's first conversation](docs/project-management.md#the-coordinators-first-conversation): on a project with no accepted workflow (tasks follow a minimal default, one type `task`: to do → work → done), the coordinator's first start sends it a first message: it reads the repository (stack, tests, CI, branches, PR host), introduces itself, sums up the project (or asks what to build) and, in that first reply, proposes a workflow with the guards that fit (often from a library example), its diff against the default, saying why (starting it counts as your request); then asks as choices what to change (stricter or lighter); setting suggestions once, never repeated; a wherdr issue or PR drafted for your yes.
- [Workspaces](docs/workspaces.md): a project of kind workspace (no git, its folder a root such as ~/work, in one home tab group) whose coordinator runs linked repositories; each is a member project with no coordinator of its own, in one workspace at most, storing only its key, name, color, machine, folder, workspace and visibility; shared settings (machines and the clone root on each, a member's clone being <root>/<repo path>, paused machines, placement, base branch, branch name template, agents and reviewer fallback, worktree setup, archive delay, delete-branch) apply unless the member overrides the field (a cleared base or branch template falls back); a workspace has its own workflow (template show/edit on it), which a member without its own runs (its Workflow and Guards tabs show the workspace's, saying so; a member's first accepted or saved workflow becomes its own); the workspace's guards apply to members between the user's and the project's, a member only hardening them; a workspace takes features only, other task types are refused; the workspace's coordinator acts on every member at the Act level with no setting (--project <member>), members get no coordinator (none started or listed), their wakes and Ask the coordinator go to the workspace's coordinator (first line naming the member task), and one autopilot counts At once and Tasks / day across members, Keep the board busy starting their to-do tasks in board order; the workspace map (wherdr pm map show/set/remove, maps/<WS>.json, rendered as map.md in the coordinator's folder) says what each repository does, talks to and is used by, written the first time a task touches a repository (no upfront reading), and map list gives every git repository under the root with an automatic one-line description (manifest description, else the README's first sentence), marked mapped or not, cached a day (--refresh); wherdr pm repo adopt <repo> makes a repository under the root a member with no approval (key, name and color proposed as the New sheet does, shared settings and workflow inherited, visibility checked, its map line naming it, written to the workspace's log and listed in the next health check), refused outside the root (symlinks resolved on the machine), for a folder already a project or another project's clone there, without git, or without an origin when the workflow pushes or opens PRs; nothing is cloned, a member runs only on machines with its clone at <root>/<repo path> (readiness check, others left out of placement); features (workspace tasks with no agent): wherdr pm feature add, feature split <WS-n> < plan.json (one call: adopts the repositories needed, adds one sub-task per repository tagged with the feature's id on the board, chains them with after and starts those that wait for nothing, all or nothing, the order's one-line reason kept on the feature), task add --feature, task edit --after (after across the workspace's projects, no cycle, no link outside it); mergeAfter (plan mergeAfter, task add/edit --merge-after, same rules) makes a sub-task's PR wait out of line in its merge queue (waits for LED-4 to be done) until those tasks are done (whole workflow: merged and deploy watched), the rest of the queue merging meanwhile, its sheet saying Merges once LED-4 is done; a stopped or abandoned upstream keeps it waiting and wakes the workspace's coordinator once; feature close once every sub-task is done or abandoned; a feature's state is derived: to do, working, waiting for you, done.
- [General tab](docs/project-management.md#general): name, coordinator name (empty: the project's name, which follows a rename; also asked at setup), other projects this coordinator may act on (Off, Read or Act), key (a new one also in wakes, notifications, logs, PR titles, `wherdr pm` outputs and new branches; texts written before the change read it too; former keys still work) and its badge color, base (working) branch, branch name template ({id}, {tag}, {type}, {slug}; default task/{id}; a branch the worker pushed is followed), Archive done tasks after (1, 3, 7, 14, 30 days or Never), Delete the task's branch after its merge (on by default), agents, worktree setup (files copied from the clone such as .env, folders such as node_modules shared only while the lockfile matches the clone's, else a setup command with a time limit; help lines above two columns of fields; Save on its own row, enabled after a change; the result in the task's log and the worker's instructions, a failure under Your turn with its output), repository visibility, allowed machines and their clone paths (each with its last readiness check, run again with ↻, and a live card: online, offline or paused, hours, a memory bar with agents, the rest, free and the reserve, cores and load or pressure, its agents with task and weight, what it takes now or why not; the board's header opens it), Shown in (the home tab showing it: Automatic with its groups, paused machines left out unless a task runs there, a group, or All tabs; a hint without groups), placement (Heavy to the strongest, Balance the load, Home first, each drawn in a small picture with one line, and the next to-do task with the machine it would go to or why it waits; a task too big for every machine runs on the best one; an idle machine always takes one task its RAM holds, the reserve holds the next ones; a worker started again is heavy only while its step takes screenshots).
- [Workflow tab](docs/project-management.md#workflow): how each task runs, read only: a chart per task type (its route in one line, cards across the width on a computer; each step's holder with its agent and model, how it ends, timeout, proofs, guard; coloured arrows for agents, the engine, your turn and the send-back loop), JSON with Copy, Ask the coordinator to change it; step kinds (landing without a remote merges into the local branch; a merge waits up to 15 minutes for its checks, or for GitHub to show its push, without holding up other tasks; after a merge, the task's remote branch is deleted when safe (merged at its head, no other open PR, not protected, a base or the default branch; else kept, with why in the log); Bitbucket Cloud PRs: bitbucket.merge, credentials from the machine; a pipeline watch follows CI or a deploy and wakes the coordinator only on a failure), an accepted change moves tasks under way by step id (a task whose step is gone goes on to the first new step it has not passed; its action runs), Save as template, review of the change the coordinator or Alfred proposed (one-line summary, who proposed it, your full request with a link back to it; the proposed workflow's chart with steps added, removed and changed marked in colour, a legend and what changes for the type's tasks, or as a list or JSON), and its Workflow change card under the turn that proposed it in the coordinator's conversation (that proposal's own changes only, the same chart compact, a tap opens the review; one card per proposal, accepted, refused or replaced); the [reviewer fallback](docs/project-management.md#reviewer-fallback) (prefs reviewFallbackAgent and reviewFallbackModel, together, any pair, none by default, checked at Save, also under the project sheet's Agents): the reviewer started instead when the review agent's account is out of quota, near it (5 h at 90 %) or held by its pace, before a start or mid-review (it reviews from the start; a Codex reviewer idle on its usage-limit message counts, its account out until the reset the message gives), each switch in the log and on the Plan's review step, the review agent again once its quota is back; the [review queue](docs/project-management.md#review-queue-and-re-reviews): 2 or 3 reviews at once per reviewer account, the others wait oldest first (*Review waits: 2 ahead on Codex*), shown in `autopilot show`; a later round reviews only the commits since the last one, a merge of the base alone is not reviewed again.
- [Guards](docs/project-management.md#guards): protected branches, who may merge (a waiting merge goes on once wherdr may do it; one you merge on GitHub ends as merged; one cut by a restart goes on by itself), contributor PRs, the project sheet's in-app addresses.
- [Automations](docs/project-management.md#automations): tasks added on a schedule or an event; the coordinator or Alfred proposes them, you accept or refuse; a list with each one's trigger in words, next firing and last results.
- [Template library](docs/project-management.md#template-library): saved templates and examples, read, rename and delete; projects keep their own copy.
- [Who sends a wake](docs/project-management.md#who-sends-a-wake): each wake's first line and chat tag name its source: Autopilot, Step check (a held step's start, recheck or timeout, even with the autopilot off; rechecks with no news back off 5m, 10m, 20m, 40m up to 1h and start over on any news on the task; the coordinator postpones with `wherdr pm step wait <task> --for <duration>|--until-user --reason`; the task sheet shows the next recheck; past the step's time limit or waiting until you write, its To do tab says what waits, for how long and the coordinator's last wait reason, with Ask the coordinator, your message to it that starts the rechecks over, then Asked), Engine (a block given up after failed fixes), Health check (every 3h by default: done, waiting for you, stalled, idle machines; acked when all is well), Incident; in the conversation a wake is a compact muted row (tag, first reason, time; tap for the full text and turn, which ends at its own end, at your next message or `!`/`/` command, or where the coordinator speaks on its own after a background task), not a bubble, with the coordinator's last answer of that turn under it, muted; consecutive routine wakes fold into one row (3 routine checks · last: "…", 08:00–11:00), holding only the wakes and their own turns, an incident or an answer asking you stays visible in its stronger colour; routine events off by default, only judgment wakes the coordinator; one kind per wake, the same ack. Skipped, and listed by `autopilot show`: a scheduled wake while nothing it could act on changed, an Engine wake for a block that is only an offline or paused machine, a second wake for a question already answered with `tell`, a health check repeating the last one (12 h at most).
- [Autopilot](docs/project-management.md#autopilot): when the project works without you, each project's own (Alfred has none), the clock header button (no workflow proposals) and its window (880 px on a computer), two tabs remembered per device: Settings (answering agent, then grouped: goal, when it wakes, limits, hours (new projects: Tasks / day unlimited and At once Auto, pace and machine room still hold automatic work; limits and hours hold automatic work only: a start you ask for goes past them, with a word, and still counts; a hint on the older 10 / 2; Task added wakes only for tasks added by someone else than this coordinator; a pinned bar with Cancel and Save, enabled by a change; leaving the tab or closing with unsaved changes asks; a project.autopilot link opens Settings) and Activity (switch, Run now, the day's timeline (24 h bar with its hours shaded, wakes sent and skipped with why, tasks started, now and the next wake; the worker's account pace gauge, go or what it waits for; the events listed, yesterday's below); Keep the board busy: the engine starts the next to-do task itself while a machine has room; the coordinator's view of machines and weights (`autopilot show`; weights learned from measured memory peaks after 3 runs; `show <task>`, `--on`, `--weight`).
- [What a task's agent said](docs/project-management.md#what-a-tasks-agent-said): `wherdr pm read`, an agent's last message or question from any machine, and the question in the wake.
- [Board](docs/project-management.md#board): the project picker (Follow machine tab, the default once groups exist; All projects; one project, shown as its key badge in its color then its name, as in every project picker; kept across devices), columns (a done or archived task is never under Your turn; Done shows only tasks not archived, newest first, its footer *N archived · show* opens the archived tasks, searchable, newest first; a task is archived after its project's delay, 7 days by default, and Unarchive brings it back), cards (the id badge copies the id; the task's machine when its project allows several), time in the step and total time, Add task (with its weight: Auto, Light, Standard, Heavy), Start, Start on another machine (its readiness check), Stop, Delete; a refused merge said in plain words (a conflict the agent is already fixing leaves Your turn).
- [What agents show in the chat](docs/project-management.md#what-agents-show-in-the-chat): every agent's *Showing instead of telling* table (situation → tool, with an example): choices and task cards for all, plus highlights, status cards, action buttons, screenshots and proposed settings for Alfred and coordinators; one card per message, blocks only in a wake, the link after a refusal, never "done" before the card says so.
- [Coordinators on other projects](docs/project-management.md#coordinators-on-other-projects): the General tab's Other projects this coordinator may act on (Off by default, Read: list, show, read, plan, incidents; Act: also task add/start/stop/edit/note/order/tag/link/check/remove, tell, report back/close), a task id names its project, `--project <KEY>` on list, plan, incidents and task add; guards, merges, approvals, settings, autopilot, workflow and automations never; the refusal names the setting; logged with the acting coordinator's name, the other coordinator told at its next wake, listed in its instructions.
- [Coordinators' notes](docs/project-management.md#coordinators-notes): `wherdr pm notes …`, a coordinator's notes: any note listed, edited, moved or removed; `notes add` defaults to the home tab its project shows in
- [Board order](docs/project-management.md#board-order): cards in board order (the coordinator's `wherdr pm task order` first, then oldest first), shared by everyone and kept across restarts; Keep the board busy, the merge queue and `wherdr pm list` follow it.
- [Spec changes](docs/project-management.md#spec-changes): when you change your mind mid-task, the coordinator's `wherdr pm task edit` (title, description, reason, diff in the log), `task note` and `tell --spec`; the worker and the reviewer read every note, the latest overriding the description; shown under the description in the task sheet; never in a wake; after several send-backs, the coordinator's `task decide <task> pass` on findings that contradict a spec change its reason cites (date or words), never before a guarded merge nor on a critical finding, shown a day in Decisions.
- [Tasks that touch the same files](docs/project-management.md#tasks-that-touch-the-same-files): declared files (files.txt, task add --files), the start that waits behind a task with the same files, Start anyway.
- [Task sheet](docs/project-management.md#task-sheet): opens over the current page from Tasks to handle, Decisions or a chat task link (`?task=ID`, kept on reload); the id badge by the title (copies the id; a long title two lines at most on a phone, whole on a tap, one line once scrolled or typing), time per step, waits for you, review rounds and CI fixes, which branch merges into which (the board card too when it is not the project's working branch), the task's PR as a badge on that line (*PR #646*, new tab; wraps under on a phone; in the sheet's header once the line scrolls away; none before a PR, not repeated under the description), the task's buttons (Open the agent whatever the step: the step's agent if it runs, else the worker, Worker or Reviewer in a menu when both run, disabled with Agent is terminated once it ended; Check on GitHub, also `wherdr pm task check`, for a stuck merge step or an archived task's PR) and its Description (Markdown), Plan (proofs in Markdown, folded, each once; a commit as a short sha linked to the Git host; a PR link as PR #12), Comments (the worker's and the reviewer's reports and verdicts in order, Markdown, folded) and History (the whole log in one timeline: hand-offs, catch-ups, CI fixes, routine lines lighter) tabs, in one scroll; on a task waiting for you, To do opens on a [TL;DR](docs/project-management.md#tldr) by Claude Haiku (at most five lines in plain words, no code names: what changes for you, what to look at on the screenshots, anything wrong; not how it was checked nor the Merge; written again once on a new prompt version, otherwise only on new commits of its own or new findings, not on a base merge, rebase or CI re-run; skipped while the pace holds automatic work, the notes shown then; an agent's question gets two or three plain lines of its own, once per question), the screenshots under it, and a link to Comments.
- [A task waiting for you](docs/project-management.md#a-task-waiting-for-you): the To do tab, Merge, Send back, Try again (each try's result in History; unreadable PR details read again, then the error with the output's last lines) and other answers; a stalled review (past its time limit, or its reviewer gone without a verdict) said in one sentence, with Restart the review (a new reviewer on the PR's latest commit), and the card's status says review pending, not ready to merge, until the review passes; a PR you merge on your Git host (I merged it, and what to do when it is not merged yet); Open the PR at the merge step for a PR a step gave as its link proof (GitHub, Bitbucket, GitLab, Azure DevOps), also on the card as PR #12; screenshots replaced after a rework (new commits since the review); a waiting PR kept up to date with its base (off Your turn and Tasks to handle while it is updated, its conflict solved or its checks fixed, with a neutral line; back once GitHub reads it clean), an approved merge that goes on by itself once ready (kept across updates, asked again only on new screenshots or interface changes; Merge stays loading on the card and the sheet until it merges or fails, with what it waits for, the same after a reload), and the project's merge queue (ready PRs merge in turn, a PR needing work steps out of line, updates only on a conflict or when GitHub requires them, all in one pass, the agent's fix pushed whatever the place, idle agents released; its place or why it stepped out on the card); a tap on Your turn or Tasks to handle opens the asking agent's conversation, else the sheet; on a phone its buttons stay pinned at the bottom of the tab, hidden while you type in a field of the sheet so nothing covers it.
- [Tasks to review, one at a time](docs/project-management.md#tasks-to-review): a task to approve with its TL;DR, newest screenshots, PR and verdict in one line, then Approve (the merge's Accept: *Approved* on the button, then the next one slides in; a fade with reduced motion; a failure stays with its error) or Reject (a note, the screenshots that are wrong and your own, file or paste, sent back to its worker, each screenshot a download with the task's key); an agent's question shows its Haiku summary, the full question folded (Markdown, as in the chat, never cut), its choices as buttons and Another answer with Send (sent to the agent, then the next task) and Open the task; a question answered anywhere (here, its conversation, a coordinator's tell) leaves at once; anything else that waits (another step of yours too) shows its To do answers (choices, Try again) and Open the task; every task has Open the agent (as on the task sheet); 3 of 12 with previous and next (a task passed over stays), keys → ← A R, All done after the last (grouped in the middle, the window shrunk to it on a computer); on a computer a 960 px window up to 90 % high, screenshots two per row, only the content scrolls; filter Follow group tab, All, a group or a project, kept across devices.
- [Notes on a task waiting for you](docs/project-management.md#notes-on-a-task-waiting-for-you): the To do tab's Worker's note (the closing report) and Reviewer's note (verdict, what was fixed during the rounds, what is left as minor), in Markdown, folded, with Show more, the task's summary above the worker's note, full width one above the other (Worker / Reviewer tabs on a phone).
- [Report a problem](docs/project-management.md#report-a-problem): tell the coordinator what is wrong with a task waiting for you, block its merge, withdraw.
- [What wherdr fixes on its own](docs/project-management.md#what-wherdr-fixes-on-its-own): a conflict with the base (to the worker), red CI (an infrastructure error in the log run again once, else to the worker), a push refused as behind its remote (synced, pushed again), a merge fixed after the fact by the clone's `wherdr.afterMerge` command, a PR updated on GitHub included (wherdr's docs/llms.txt: one line per entry), an interrupted action (run again), a stalled agent, a task nobody moves (one task's error never stops the others; quiet 20 min with no stated reason: its stuck or never-started action, or its merge, run again, looked at after 40, 80 min…, the coordinator woken once per step; a hung step action freed after 30 min, its late result only logged); the coordinator woken once only after 2 failed tries, with what was tried.
- [A stalled task](docs/project-management.md#a-stalled-task): red CI or an idle agent: one nudge, a restart 10 min later, the coordinator woken 10 min after that, then Tasks to review and a notification after 30 min; a stall or a step past its time limit leaves Tasks to review once the task is back to work (on a coordinator-held step, Ask the coordinator does it: Waiting for the coordinator to check the deploy, then Asked); a step's time limit stops counting while its machine is offline, an incident is open or the task waits for room (the card shows what it waits for).
- [Why agents are gone](docs/project-management.md#why-agents-are-gone): the engine's cause from facts (machine offline, herdr-core or wherdr restarted, agent killed or crashed, out of memory, account limit, unknown), recorded as an incident per machine; `wherdr pm incidents [--since]`, the last open one in `autopilot show`.
- [The engine resumes the work](docs/project-management.md#the-engine-resumes-the-work): a task an incident stopped waits for wherdr (not Your turn) and is resumed once the cause is gone (restart or crash at once, machine back online, account limit reset): its worker in its worktree, Claude's conversation resumed, else a new agent with a handover; the tasks before it first, its followers *Waits for <task> to resume*; placement, room and pace held, one worker per task; the same cause again within an hour of a resume is not resumed again.
- [The incident wake](docs/project-management.md#the-incident-wake): one wake per incident (not per task) once the engine's resumes settle, to each project's coordinator and to Alfred for all projects: the cause and its evidence, what was resumed, what still waits and why (machine offline, limit until <time>), what needs the coordinator or the user; never state a cause not read: `wherdr pm incidents`, `autopilot show`, `read <task>` first, else 'unknown' and what was checked.
- [A task's temporary files](docs/project-management.md#a-tasks-temporary-files): `.wherdr-tmp` in the task's worktree (TMPDIR, CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR, NODE_COMPILE_CACHE), ignored by git, removed with the worktree; no agent started while /tmp has under 500 MB free.
- [Processes an agent leaves behind](docs/project-management.md#processes-an-agent-leaves-behind): ending an agent kills its terminal's process tree and groups (TERM, then KILL after 3 s); every 5 minutes and at start, processes an agent started (known by the task's .wherdr-tmp they inherit, never by their folder alone; on macOS, sh/zsh/sleep with their marked parent or group, or re-parented in the task's worktree; never the user's own shells, apps or daemons) are killed once their task has no live agent, and logged on the task; removing a worktree kills what works in it first; a CPU guard kills a task's process above 80 % CPU for 20 min after its agent ended (tells the coordinator while it runs); Settings › Machines says *n leftover processes killed*; the wherdr template's workers run test commands that could hang with a timeout.
- [Alfred's command](docs/alfred.md): `wherdr alfred`, what Alfred reads and changes after your yes or a card's Apply (told back to it, so it goes on by itself; projects, their machines, guards, coordinators started or resumed, lines added to a coordinator's memory.md, settings, all v2 projects in one card), the workflow changes it proposes for your review, and its messages to a project's coordinator (`tell`, `last`).
- [Agents of a task that waits for you](docs/project-management.md#agents-of-a-task-that-waits-for-you): idle agents ended and started again, at once when you answer (a decision, Send back, Try again), a worker that ended too; a watchdog starts again the agent of a task under way missing for 3 minutes (after a restart too), else the card says why and the coordinator is woken once at the second failure; kept while the worker updates the PR (a catch-up, a CI fix), a worker that ended started again with that work (once), else the card says why it waits (its machine offline or paused, no room on it, its agent ended) and the coordinator is woken (none: Your turn; no room: only after 30 minutes of it), unpushed commits pushed first; which agent a coordinator's `tell` reaches (--to worker|reviewer); in a wake, `tell --fix base|ci|machine|stall --reason` unblocks a mechanical block (autopilot on, twice per task and step, logged; at any step an ended worker starts again with it while its worktree is there; at the review step a reviewer not running starts the review again), a permission request stays yours; a failed step action handed over with `--fix` leaves Tasks to review (*the agent is fixing it*), is tried again once the worker is done, and comes back with the new reason if it fails again or the worker stops without a report. One worker and one reviewer per task: a second start at once is refused (already starting), a held start dropped, a duplicate agent ended and logged.
- [Notes](docs/alfred.md#notes): `wherdr alfred notes` and `wherdr pm notes` (list, show, add, edit, remove, file put, file remove): short whiteboard notes agents write and the user reads, scoped to all or one home tab (a group or a machine shown as its own tab), linking to other notes, files under `notes/` or in-app places, with project badges `[[KEY-12]]` and custom badges `[[label|icon|colour|link]]`; any coordinator may list, edit, move and remove any note, adding to its project's tab by default, and changes another project's note only when outdated or asked; every change logged with who made it
- [Suggestions](docs/alfred.md#suggestions): Alfred and coordinators suggest a setting you may like once (`ui open --target`), never again if ignored; when wherdr cannot do what you need, they may draft an issue or PR on wherdr's repository, with no private data, posted only on your yes.
- [Updating wherdr](docs/alfred.md#updating-wherdr): the banner's Update with Alfred sends `Update wherdr to <version>: <release URL>`; for any update Alfred reads update-with-an-agent.md and the release notes, never from memory.
- [After an update](docs/alfred.md#after-an-update): new instructions for Alfred and coordinators, and the one-line notice on their next command (also after a rebuild from a new commit); they read the running build's docs wherever wherdr was started from; Alfred gives the server's real address and port, and server commands as text to copy, never *Run*.

## Machines, quotas and notifications

- [Several machines](docs/machines.md#several-machines-ssh): machines reached by hc over SSH; the host shown by its host name with a HOST badge; New preselects a machine of the current tab.
- [Before adding a machine](docs/machines.md#before-adding-a-machine): what a machine needs first.
- [Manage machines](docs/machines.md#manage-machines): Settings › Machines (one card per machine: name, state, actions, keep awake, memory), add, reconnect, rename, forget, keep awake (until a time or turned off, laptop battery and lid warning), capacity (memory, cores, load on Linux and macOS; swap on Linux; on macOS memory pressure first, then macOS's own available estimate, its free percentage of the RAM, with a 10 % reserve), memory limits (an idle machine always takes one task its RAM holds, the minimum free holds the next ones), available hours and offline machines (an automatic start that finds its machine unreachable waits and starts once it is back), and where each start goes (placement across a project's machines).
- [Pause a machine for a project](docs/machines.md#pause-a-machine-for-a-project): a machine's on/off switch in a project's Machines list: no new task there, running ones finish, clone kept; Paused in every project in Settings › Machines.
- [Claude and Codex quotas](docs/quotas.md#claude-and-codex-quotas): remaining usage per account, with the machines sharing it (one Codex account stays one row when a machine is idle or a read fails), and its setup; a Codex 'Limit reached' past its reset reads as reset, credits show and let work go on, an old reading says how to refresh it. [Codex updates](docs/quotas.md#codex-updates): Codex starts with its update check off; a message sent while it installs or updates waits and is typed once it is ready (back into the field if it exits); a Codex that exits after updating itself keeps its space, with a Your turn card (Resume conversation, Start fresh).
- [Pace](docs/quotas.md#pace): Settings › Agents › Pace, its modes (Free, the default, stops only at the account's own limit), when automatic work may start, and the end-of-week burn (one switch: no pace limit until the weekly reset, then off); a reviewer account held by its pace hands new reviews to the reviewer fallback.
- [Notifications](docs/notifications.md#notifications): Web Push and Do not disturb.
- [A default and exceptions](docs/notifications.md#a-default-and-exceptions): one synced policy: a default and its exceptions, a coordinator's kept across restarts.
- [Notifications on hc](docs/core.md#notifications): when v3 sends a push, from hc's events.

## Extending and fixing

- [Plugins](docs/plugins.md#wherdr-plugins): optional page plugins and how to install them.
- [The plugin module](docs/plugins.md#the-module): what a plugin file exports.
- [Markers](docs/plugins.md#markers-data-wherdr): `data-wherdr` markers a plugin can find.
- [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md#troubleshooting): hc connection, conversations, machines and network problems.
- [Setup on hc](docs/core.md#setup): `HC_SOCKET`, the hc endpoint wherdr talks to.

## Contributors

- [Development and tests](docs/development.md): run from source and test.
- [Design rules](docs/design.md): the interface styling reference, sheets included (where focus goes on open); nothing scrolls sideways (no negative horizontal margin without an `overflow-safe` reason); one scroll per sheet, which ends at the sheet's bottom edge (the bottom gap is padding inside it); the app's thin scrollbars, never the browser's.
- [Dictation design](docs/dictation.md): the dictation engines and how to add one; the on-device model cards (each model's best languages and their quality, the device's language marked); why a server-side model install fails (missing decompressor, disk full; .tar.bz2 needs no bzip2, a JS decoder unpacks it); read aloud and its voices (iOS gives web apps only its standard voices); the neural voice catalog (Siwis, Cori, MLS) and its engine (streamed WebAudio playback, fallback to the device's voices); the Voice of wherdr setting (install a French or English voice, each reply read in its guessed language).
- [Read aloud: the voice of wherdr](docs/read-aloud.md): the on-device voices (Siwis, Cori, MLS), their licences and the attribution shown; espeak-ng (GPL) inside the pinned sherpa-onnx 1.12.x runtime; the memory budget (measured heap, else an estimate); the iPhone 13 measurements of Siwis and Cori (load, first sentence, real-time factor; Heap is the runtime's 512 MiB WASM memory, not the voice's own use); how to measure with Test (download, load, first sentence, real-time factor, heap).

- [The wherdr command](docs/command.md): the 2.x npm and Homebrew packages and service.
